A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same honorific-usage study. All 13 pages, including Appendices A–F, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original analyses of Bengali and Hindi Wikipedia articles, including honorific frequencies, statistical associations and human validation of GPT-4o annotations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original Wikipedia analyses and human-validation results, with corrections to three reported Bengali agreement values.

M1.justification: GPT-4o annotation, chi-squared analysis and logistic regression remain unchanged, as do the annotation prompts and feature categories.

E1.justification: Both versions analyze the same Bengali and Hindi Wikipedia coverage of real, fictional and mythological beings. Dataset composition in Table 2 is identical.

E2.justification: The same GPT-4o and human-annotator comparisons appear in Table 3 and Figures 5–6. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain first-paragraph analysis and validation on 100 randomly selected articles per language by two native speakers. No sampling, metric or evaluation-procedure change is reported.

E4.justification: The feature-association analyses, regression analysis, illustrative entity examples and supplementary analyses are unchanged. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Agreement percentages, kappa reporting and chi-squared significance testing follow the same practices. The corrected agreement-statistic values affect E6, without changing statistical procedures or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Section 3 changes Bengali inter-annotator kappa from 0.95 to 0.89, retaining 98% agreement. GPT-4o–human agreement changes from 97% to 85%, and kappa from 0.93 to 0.47. These localized corrections align with unchanged Table 3 and Figure 6; all other results remain identical.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and the descriptions of chi-squared analysis and logistic regression are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty claims, cross-language findings, Hindi gender-bias claim and claims about LLM usefulness for sociolinguistic research.

C2.justification: Sociocultural interpretations and stated limitations are identical. Section 3 still says the agreement results demonstrate GPT-4o reliability despite the lower corrected Bengali values.

D1.justification: Sampling descriptions, annotation instructions, prompt details and annotator demographics in Section 3 and Appendices D–F are unchanged. No reproducibility or resource-access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list and the positioning relative to previous honorific and sociolinguistic research are identical.

P1.justification: Apart from the three numerical substitutions, the wording, headings, paragraph organization and appendix structure are identical.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions and page layouts are unchanged. Visual comparison localizes the differences to the three substituted numerical values in Section 3.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects overstated Bengali validation figures in Section 3 to match evidence already present in Table 3 and Figure 6. This improves internal consistency and reporting accuracy. The improvement is limited because the unqualified interpretation of GPT-4o reliability remains unchanged.
